EXPLANATORY EXTRACT FROM THE FRONTISPIECE 


ANNALS OF COLLECTIVE ECONOMY . . . 1962 


The Annals of Collective Economy were founded in 1908, as a French-language 
publication (Annales de l'économie collective), by Edgard Milhaud. 


The English issue has been published since 1925, as has the German issue (Annalen 
der Gemeinwirtschaft). 


Until April 1960 Edgard Milhaud was director of the three issues. 


Since 1947, the Annals have been the official review of the International Centre 
of Research and Information on Collective Economy (ICRICE). 


The expression "collective economy", as used by the ICRICE and in the Annals, covers 
all economic activities intended to render a service directly to the community. Both 
the ICRICE and the Annals are concerned with the following problems: 


economic action by the State, national and regional planning; 
activities of municipal authorities; 

public enterprise; 

co-operation; 

the role of the trade unions in the economic field. 


The work of Edgard Milhaud, the founder of the ICRICE, has aroused so much interest 
in different parts of the world that many municipal authorities, co-operatives and 
trade unions have voluntarily come forward to offer their aid. 


In addition to the united efforts of all these bodies, the Centre is aided by its 
national sections (in Austria, Belgium, France, the Federal Republic of Germany, Greece, 
Italy, Luxembourg, Switzerland and Yugoslavia. 


In addition, the Fondation universitaire de Belgique has been assisting the Centre 
with the publication of the Annals since 1962. 


ANNALS OF COLLECTIVE ECONOMY
